summary.en-US: Switch proxy profiles in one click. Keep page-visible location, timezone and WebRTC settings together, with clear identity diagnostics. For Firefox desktop.

description.en-US:
One profile for your proxy and browser identity.

Net Identity brings proxy routing, page-visible geolocation, timezone and WebRTC settings into one profile. Use it for regional website testing, checking timezone-sensitive web apps, or switching between repeatable browser setups. Bring your own proxy: the extension does not provide proxy servers or a VPN service.

Switch quickly. Check what is actually applied.

  • One-click profiles. Choose a saved proxy profile, use Firefox's normal routing with Direct, or turn the extension's identity controls Off.
  • Automatic or manual identity. Resolve approximate location and timezone from the observed public egress IP, or choose your own coordinates and IANA timezone. GeoIP lookups can be disabled.
  • Clear diagnostics. See the selected route, available public IP and identity details, WebRTC policy, and consistency checks. Unverified or unavailable information is shown explicitly.
  • Edit without surprises. Save profile changes first, then Apply the saved configuration when you are ready to switch.
  • Flexible proxy settings. Use HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4 or SOCKS5, configure bypass rules, and use supported proxy authentication with session-only credentials.
  • A map when you choose. Load a real OpenFreeMap basemap to help choose manual coordinates. Pan, zoom, click or drag the marker. The coordinate grid and typed coordinates also work offline, and no map data is requested until you load it.


Get started

  1. Open Net Identity and choose Add / Manage profiles.
  2. Enter your proxy details and choose automatic or manual identity settings.
  3. Save, then Apply. Open Details in the popup to inspect the result.


Privacy and control

No telemetry, analytics or remotely loaded code. Proxy usernames and passwords are held for the current Firefox session and are sent only to the selected proxy for authentication; they are not saved in durable profile storage or shared with web pages or the GeoIP provider. You may need to enter them again after Firefox exits.

When enabled, automatic identity lookup contacts ipwho.is. A proxied request shows the provider the proxy's public IP. A lookup using Direct can expose your own public IP and waits for optional data-collection permission. These requests send no proxy credentials, cookies or referrer. Installing the extension alone does not start a lookup.

Optional online map. Choosing Load online map sends your connection's public IP and the viewed map area to OpenFreeMap and its delivery infrastructure, which may include Cloudflare. Requests use the currently applied route, not unsaved proxy edits. Direct or Off also requires Firefox's optional public-IP permission. You can unload the map and continue working with coordinates offline.

Know the limits

Firefox 140 or newer on desktop is required. Direct uses Firefox and system routing, so an existing browser or system proxy may still apply. GeoIP locations are approximate. Page-level timezone and geolocation changes are observable compatibility shims; they do not make you anonymous or invisible to fingerprinting. Some sandboxed frames cannot be modified. Review your bypass rules and the audit before relying on a profile. For HTTP/HTTPS account identity, the proxy server must require authentication: configured credentials alone do not prove which account handled a request if the endpoint accepts anonymous CONNECT.

Firefox does not let extensions cancel protected browser-service requests. The extension blocks ordinary web-page traffic when required proxy credentials are missing, but the same proxy could accept protected browser traffic anonymously. If proxy-account identity must hold across the whole browser, configure your proxy server to reject anonymous access. This extension is not a browser-wide network kill switch.

Open source under the MIT license.

privacy_policy.en-US:
Privacy

net-identity does not include telemetry, analytics, or remotely loaded program code.

What is stored on this computer

  • Profiles and non-secret applied route: name, proxy host, authentication-required flag, location, timezone and WebRTC choice are kept in Firefox extension storage (storage.local) until you delete the profile or extension.
  • Proxy username and password: kept in Firefox session storage until Firefox exits.
  • Active routing snapshot: includes credentials needed after the background page restarts; kept in Firefox session storage until Firefox exits.


Neither a username nor a password is written into the saved or applied profile. Schema 4 converts legacy usernames to a non-secret authentication-required flag. Migration removes secret keys from supported documents that can be migrated safely. Newer or unsafe documents are left unchanged and held inactive, rather than silently dropping a profile or its proxy.

What leaves this computer

Location lookup. Activating or refreshing a profile can ask https://ipwho.is/ where the current connection appears to come from. The request sends no cookies, no referrer, and no explicit proxy credentials. A proxied profile shows that service the proxy's public address. Browser routing shows it your own public address, and only after you allow that collection in Firefox. Installing the extension does not create a profile, so a fresh install makes no such request. Coordinates from this lookup are approximate (about 20 km) and are not presented as GPS.

Location picker. The picker starts with a local coordinate grid and makes no map request until you choose Load online map for the current editor session. MapLibre program code, CSS and its worker ship with the extension. Only map data comes from https://tiles.openfreemap.org: styles, tile metadata, vector/raster tiles, sprites and font glyphs are requested as needed. Panning and zooming can fetch additional data. This is separate from GeoIP lookup; disabling GeoIP does not cancel an explicitly enabled online map.

OpenFreeMap and its delivery infrastructure, which may include Cloudflare, can see your network-visible IP, the viewed map region encoded in tile coordinates, and normal HTTP metadata. No separate profile or marker upload occurs, and proxy credentials are not sent to the map provider; the viewed region is nevertheless not private from that provider. Requests omit cookies, origin credentials and referrers, reject redirects and stay within the approved provider URL policy. No device-location API, geocoder, API key or account is used. The extension does not spoof a Referer or web origin.

Map requests use the currently applied route, not unsaved proxy edits. An active proxy remains authoritative; failure does not trigger Direct. Provider-host bypass rules refuse online-map loading rather than silently overriding a bypass. Under Direct or Off, optional personal-data permission is required before loading, and Firefox/system proxy settings may still affect the visible IP. Route changes, permission revocation or closing the editor invalidate the map session. Unload the map to stop further map requests. Typed coordinates and the local grid remain usable when the map is disabled, unavailable or cannot render with WebGL.

OpenFreeMap's privacy policy states that ordinary logs exclude IP addresses, anonymized service metadata may be retained indefinitely, and security-incident IP logs may be kept for up to 30 days. Cloudflare may process requests under its own policy. See the provider's terms. The extension makes no claim that the provider collects nothing.

Proxy traffic. Traffic you choose to send through a proxy goes to that proxy. The extension does not add its own analytics to that traffic. If a selected proxy fails, ordinary external traffic fails rather than switching to Firefox's direct or system route. The selected profile stays selected and can recover without a route switch. After a full Firefox exit, session-only usernames and passwords are lost; if the applied profile requires authentication, non-bypassed ordinary webpage and extension-observable GeoIP requests are blocked until you save replacement credentials and Apply them. The request gate prevents those ordinary requests from trying that endpoint anonymously, even if the proxy would accept it: anonymous access could produce a different egress identity. Profiles intentionally configured without authentication and explicit bypasses keep their existing behavior.

Proxy transport security. Session-only storage does not encrypt the connection to a proxy. SOCKS5 username/password authentication is plaintext on that connection (RFC 1929); HTTP proxy Basic authentication likewise needs a protected transport. HTTPS to a destination does not by itself encrypt the preceding SOCKS authentication. Use only a trusted proxy and a suitably protected network path. This extension does not add an encrypted tunnel.

HTTP/HTTPS proxy account identity. The proxy server must enforce authentication. Saving or applying session credentials alone does not prove which account handled a request. An HTTP/HTTPS endpoint that accepts anonymous CONNECT without a proxy-authentication challenge (407) can carry ordinary webpage or map requests anonymously. If a specific account must be used, configure the proxy to reject anonymous access and verify the effective account at the proxy. This limitation is separate from the protected Firefox browser-service requests described below.

What pages can see

Pages receive the location and timezone of the active profile through compatibility shims. Those shims are visible to a page that inspects them. They are not a claim that the browser is anonymous or undetectable. A frame Firefox will not inject into can still see the computer's timezone and location.

Your choices

  • Do not activate a profile, and the extension does not contact the GeoIP service.
  • Leave the online map disabled to avoid OpenFreeMap requests. Unload it or close the editor to stop its session without changing the active identity.
  • Use a proxy profile when the location lookup should see the proxy's address.
  • Use Custom identity policies for manual coordinates, a timezone override, unavailable geolocation, or disabled GeoIP lookup. Disabled GeoIP makes no GeoIP provider request; separately enabled online-map requests are independent.
  • Direct switches routing immediately even without optional consent. It keeps native geolocation blocked until Off; identity is unavailable until a permitted lookup succeeds.
  • Save stores edits; Apply activates the saved configuration and leaves unsaved form edits alone. An event-page restart preserves the applied revision and credentials, including when a newer revision was saved. Leaving both username and password blank keeps existing session credentials; entering either replaces the pair, and Clear credentials removes the saved credentials (Apply also removes them from runtime).
  • Deactivate the profile to stop the shims and release the WebRTC setting.


Passive health observations

The background temporarily correlates at most 512 request IDs with the selected SOCKS endpoint, route generation and destination hostname. It keeps no URL path/query, headers or event-provided credentials. Samples expire after 30 seconds, failure evidence uses a five-second window, and everything is in memory, not durable storage or telemetry. These observations can indicate suspected trouble but cannot identify its transport cause. No diagnostic probe or automatic HTTP retry is sent. Credentials you supply are transmitted only to your selected proxy for authentication, never to the GeoIP provider or page scripts.

Firefox consent

Required locationInfo describes approximate egress location lookup and the viewed map area requested from OpenFreeMap. Required authenticationInfo describes the existing credentials sent to your chosen proxy. Optional personallyIdentifyingInfo gates Direct/Off online-map loading and direct GeoIP requests that can expose your own public IP. OpenFreeMap is an additional recipient only when you explicitly enable the online map. The earlier authentication declaration disclosed an existing proxy-authentication recipient; it did not itself add a new recipient or telemetry. Firefox may show changed required-data consent on installation or update. These built-in controls require desktop Firefox 140 or later. Mozilla's data taxonomy explains the categories.

Protected Firefox requests

Firefox does not let extensions cancel every browser-service request. In Firefox 158, protected Remote Settings traffic could still reach the same selected proxy anonymously when the session credential pair was missing. This is not a switch to Direct, but a proxy that accepts anonymous clients may assign a different egress identity. Ordinary permitted webpage traffic and observable GeoIP requests remain covered by the missing-credential gate. For account identity across all browser traffic, configure the proxy server to reject anonymous access. The extension is not a browser-wide kill switch and does not change OS firewalls or Firefox security settings.

captions: Switch profiles and review the current identity in one compact popup
Manage proxy profiles and save identity settings before applying them
Inspect routing, WebRTC policy and identity checks, including unverified states
Choose manual coordinates on an optional OpenFreeMap basemap, with visible attribution
